topics.title: Overview, Objectives & Key Definitions
topics.concept:
Unit Overview

Having learned how to differentiate, this unit is about what derivatives mean in the real world. A derivative is a rate of change, and interpreting it correctly — with units and direction — is a core AP skill. You will study motion (position, velocity, acceleration), related rates (how linked quantities change together in time), linearization (using a tangent line to approximate), and L'Hôpital's Rule (using derivatives to resolve indeterminate limits).

This unit is heavy on interpretation and problem set-up. On the exam it is a frequent source of free-response questions.

Big picture: A derivative carries units of output per unit of input and tells you both how fast and which direction a quantity is changing.

Learning Objectives

  • Interpret a derivative's value, sign, and units in context.
  • Analyze rectilinear motion: relate position, velocity, acceleration, speed, and displacement.
  • Set up and solve related-rates problems.
  • Use local linearity / linearization to approximate function values.
  • Apply L'Hôpital's Rule to indeterminate forms 0/0 and ∞/∞.

Prerequisite Concepts

  • Fluent differentiation, especially the Chain Rule (Unit 3) — essential for related rates.
  • Geometry formulas (area, volume, Pythagoras, similar triangles).
  • Indeterminate forms from Unit 1.

Key Definitions

  • Rate of change in context: f'(a) has units of (units of f) per (unit of x); its sign tells direction (increasing/decreasing).
  • Velocity: v(t) = s'(t). Acceleration: a(t) = v'(t) = s''(t). Speed: |v(t)|.
  • Displacement: net change in position. At rest: v(t) = 0.
  • Related rates: quantities linked by an equation, each changing with time; differentiate the relation with respect to t.
  • Linearization of f at a: L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x − a) (the tangent-line approximation).
  • Indeterminate form: an expression like 0/0 or ∞/∞ whose value is not determined by the parts alone.

quiz.q: The volume of water in a tank is V(t) liters after t minutes. What are the units of V'(t)?
quiz.explanation: A derivative has units of (units of output) per (unit of input): liters per minute.

quiz.q: A cup of coffee cools so that its temperature is T(t) degrees Celsius after t minutes. T'(5) = -2 means:
options: The coffee is cooling at 2 C per minute at t = 5
The coffee is 2 C at t = 5
The coffee is warming at 2 C per minute
quiz.explanation: A negative derivative means the quantity is decreasing; T'(5) = -2 means the temperature is falling at 2 C per minute at t = 5.

quiz.q: The height of a plant is h(t) cm after t days. h'(t) represents:
options: The growth rate of the plant in cm per day
quiz.explanation: h'(t) is the instantaneous rate of change of height with respect to time, i.e., the growth rate in cm/day.

quiz.q: A particle moves with position s(t) = t^2 - 4t. What is its velocity function v(t)?
quiz.explanation: Velocity is the derivative of position: v(t) = s'(t) = 2t - 4.

quiz.q: If v(t) is velocity, what is the acceleration a(t)?
quiz.explanation: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity: a(t) = v'(t) = s''(t).

topics.title: Important Theorems & Formulas
topics.concept:
Important Theorems / Rules

L'Hôpital's Rule: If lim f/g gives 0/0 or ∞/∞ and the limits of f' and g' behave, then lim f(x)/g(x) = lim f'(x)/g'(x). Check the indeterminate form before applying; a form like 1/0 is not indeterminate.

Speeding up / slowing down: a particle is speeding up when v and a have the same sign, and slowing down when they have opposite signs.

Important Theorems / Rules

L'Hôpital's Rule: If lim f/g gives 0/0 or ∞/∞ and the limits of f' and g' behave, then lim f(x)/g(x) = lim f'(x)/g'(x). Check the indeterminate form before applying; a form like 1/0 is not indeterminate.

Speeding up / slowing down: a particle is speeding up when v and a have the same sign, and slowing down when they have opposite signs.

Important Formulas

  • Linearization: L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x − a); differential dy = f'(x) dx.
  • Common related-rates relations (differentiate w.r.t. t):
    • Circle area A = πr² → dA/dt = 2πr (dr/dt)
    • Sphere volume V = (4/3)πr³ → dV/dt = 4πr² (dr/dt)
    • Cube volume V = s³ → dV/dt = 3s² (ds/dt)
    • Right-triangle / Pythagoras x² + y² = z² → 2x(dx/dt) + 2y(dy/dt) = 2z(dz/dt)

quiz.q: If C(x) is the cost in dollars to produce x items, what does C'(200) = 3 mean?
options: Producing the 200th item costs about $3 more (marginal cost is $3/item)
quiz.explanation: C'(x) is the marginal cost, the approximate cost of producing one additional item. C'(200) = 3 means the cost is rising by about $3 per item at x = 200.

quiz.q: A population P(t) satisfies P(10) = 5000 and P'(10) = 120. Approximately what is P(11)?
quiz.explanation: Using the local linear approximation, P(11) ≈ P(10) + P'(10)(1) = 5000 + 120 = 5120.

quiz.q: If f'(a) > 0 at a point a, what can be concluded about f near a?
options: f has a maximum at a
quiz.explanation: A positive derivative indicates that the function is increasing at that point.

quiz.q: The number of bacteria is N(t) after t hours. If N'(3) = 400, the units are:
quiz.explanation: The derivative measures how fast the count changes with time: bacteria per hour.

quiz.q: A particle has position s(t) = t^2 - 4t. At what time t is the particle at rest?
quiz.explanation: The particle is at rest when v(t) = 2t - 4 = 0, which gives t = 2.

topics.title: Concept Explanations & Solved Examples
topics.concept:
Concept Explanations

Interpreting derivatives (4.1). Always attach units and read the sign. If T(t) is temperature in °C after t minutes, then T'(5) = −2 means "cooling at 2 °C per minute at t = 5." A second derivative describes how the rate itself is changing (e.g., increasing at a decreasing rate).

Motion (4.2). Differentiate position to get velocity, again to get acceleration. Watch the distinction between displacement (integral/net of velocity, can be negative) and total distance (accounts for turnarounds where v = 0). Use the same-sign rule to decide speeding up vs. slowing down.

Related rates (4.4–4.5) — the standard method:

  1. Draw and label; identify which rates are given and which is wanted.
  2. Write an equation relating the variables (geometry).
  3. Differentiate both sides with respect to t (Chain Rule everywhere).
  4. Substitute the known instantaneous values last — never before differentiating.
  5. Solve for the unknown rate; include units.

Linearization (4.6). Near x = a, a smooth curve looks like its tangent line. Use L(x) to approximate hard values (e.g., √4.1 ≈ 2.025). For a concave-up function the tangent lies below the curve, so the estimate is an underestimate; concave-down gives an overestimate.

L'Hôpital's Rule (4.7). When substitution yields 0/0 or ∞/∞, differentiate top and bottom separately and re-evaluate; repeat if still indeterminate. It elegantly recovers the fundamental limits, e.g. lim_{x→0} sin x / x = lim cos x / 1 = 1.

Worked Examples

Example 1 (Motion — distance). For s(t) = t³ − 6t² + 9t + 1, find total distance on [0, 2]. v(t) = 3(t−1)(t−3), so it turns at t = 1. s(0) = 1, s(1) = 5, s(2) = 3. Distance = |5 − 1| + |3 − 5| = 4 + 2 = 6.

Example 2 (Speeding up?). v(t) = t² − 4, a(t) = 2t. At t = 3: v = 5 > 0 and a = 6 > 0 — same sign — so the particle is speeding up.

Example 3 (Related rates — balloon). Air enters a sphere at 100 cm³/s. How fast is r growing when r = 5? dV/dt = 4πr²(dr/dt) → 100 = 4π(25)(dr/dt) = 100π(dr/dt) → dr/dt = 1/π cm/s.

Example 4 (Related rates — ladder). A 10-ft ladder's base slides out at 2 ft/s. When the base is 6 ft out, the top is 8 ft up. 2x·x' + 2y·y' = 0 → 2(6)(2) + 2(8)(y') = 0 → y' = −1.5 ft/s (sliding down).

Example 5 (Linearization). Approximate √4.1 with f(x) = √x at a = 4: f'(4) = 1/4, so L(4.1) = 2 + (1/4)(0.1) = 2.025.

Example 6 (L'Hôpital). lim_{x→0} (1 − cos x)/x² = (0/0) → lim sin x/(2x) = (0/0) → lim cos x/2 = 1/2.

quiz.q: A particle moves along a line with s(t) = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t. On what interval is the particle moving to the right (v > 0)?
quiz.explanation: v(t) = 3t^2 - 12t + 9 = 3(t - 1)(t - 3). This is positive when t < 1 or t > 3.

quiz.q: The position of an object is s(t) = -16t^2 + 64t (feet). What is its velocity at t = 1 second?
An object is thrown upward with s(t) = -16t^2 + 64t. At what time does it reach its maximum height?
quiz.explanation: Maximum height occurs when v(t) = -32t + 64 = 0, giving t = 2 seconds.

quiz.q: The speed of a particle is defined as:
quiz.explanation: Speed is the magnitude of velocity, |v(t)|; it is always nonnegative and ignores direction.

quiz.q: A spherical balloon's volume is V = (4/3) pi r^3. The rate dV/dr equals:
quiz.explanation: d/dr [(4/3) pi r^3] = (4/3) pi * 3 r^2 = 4 pi r^2 (which is the surface area).

topics.title: Graphical Interpretation, Common Mistakes & Tips
topics.concept:
Graphical Interpretation

  • The velocity graph's sign shows direction of motion; its zeros mark turning points; its own slope is acceleration.
  • Linearization is literally the tangent line; the approximation error grows with distance from a and with the curve's concavity.
  • A quantity increasing at a decreasing rate has f' > 0, f'' < 0 — rising but leveling off.

Common Mistakes

  • Omitting units or misreading the sign of a rate in context.
  • Confusing displacement with total distance (forgetting to split at v = 0).
  • Substituting numbers before differentiating in related rates — this freezes variables that are actually changing.
  • Forgetting the Chain Rule (dr/dt, dh/dt, …) when differentiating a related-rates relation.
  • Applying L'Hôpital to a non-indeterminate form (e.g., 1/0), or forgetting to re-check the form after one application.

AP Exam Tips

  • Related-rates and motion questions are free-response staples — practice clean set-ups and always state units.
  • Justify "speeding up/slowing down" by comparing the signs of v and a explicitly.
  • For approximations, state the linearization and note whether it's an over- or under-estimate using concavity.
  • Confirm the indeterminate form in writing before using L'Hôpital's Rule.

Unit Summary

  • A derivative in context has units and a sign — interpret both.
  • Motion: v = s', a = v'; speed = |v|; distance splits at v = 0; same-sign v, a ⇒ speeding up.
  • Related rates: relate → differentiate in t → substitute last.
  • Linearization L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x − a) approximates near a; concavity decides over/under.
  • L'Hôpital's Rule resolves 0/0 and ∞/∞ by differentiating top and bottom.

Next unit: use derivatives to analyze the shape of graphs — extrema, concavity, and optimization.

quiz.q: Water flows into a tank at a rate R(t) = t^2 gallons per minute. What does R'(t) represent?
options: How fast the inflow rate itself is changing (gallons per minute per minute)
The total gallons in the tank
The gallons per minute flowing in
quiz.explanation: R(t) is already a rate (gallons/min). Its derivative R'(t) is the rate of change of that rate, with units gallons per minute per minute.

quiz.q: A particle has v(t) = t^2 - 4 and a(t) = 2t. At t = 3, is the particle speeding up or slowing down?
options: Speeding up (v and a are both positive)
quiz.explanation: At t = 3: v(3) = 5 > 0 and a(3) = 6 > 0. Since velocity and acceleration have the same sign, the particle is speeding up.

quiz.q: A particle has velocity v(t) = t^2 - 2t. At t = 3, the particle is:
quiz.explanation: v(3) = 9 - 6 = 3 > 0 (moving right). a(t) = 2t - 2, so a(3) = 4 > 0. Same sign as v, so speeding up.

quiz.q: A particle has position s(t) = t^3 - 3t^2 - 9t. On what interval is it slowing down?
quiz.explanation: v(t) = 3t^2 - 6t - 9 = 3(t-3)(t+1), zero at t = -1, 3. a(t) = 6t - 6, zero at t = 1. Slowing down where v and a have opposite signs: for t < -1 (v>0? check: at t=-2 v=3(−5)(−1)=15>0, a=−18<0 → opposite → slowing) and 1 < t < 3 (v<0, a>0 → opposite → slowing).

quiz.q: The temperature of an object is T(t) = 20 + 60e^(-0.1t) degrees. What is the rate of temperature change at t = 0?

mock_tests.title: Practice Set A

questions.q: For the area of a circle A = pi r^2, what is dA/dt in terms of dr/dt?
questions.explanation: Differentiating A = pi r^2 with respect to t: dA/dt = 2 pi r (dr/dt).

questions.q: In a related-rates problem, the first step is usually to:
options: Write an equation relating the variables, then differentiate with respect to time
questions.explanation: You relate the quantities with an equation, differentiate implicitly with respect to t, and only then substitute the known instantaneous values.

questions.q: The linearization of f at x = a is given by:
questions.explanation: The linearization (tangent-line approximation) at x = a is L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x - a).

questions.q: L'Hopital's Rule can be applied directly to a limit only when it has which indeterminate form?
questions.explanation: L'Hopital's Rule applies to indeterminate quotients of the form 0/0 or infinity/infinity.

questions.q: If g(x) measures the distance (miles) traveled after x hours, the units of g'(x) are:
questions.explanation: The derivative gives distance per unit time: miles per hour (a speed).

questions.q: A particle moving along a line is momentarily at rest when:
questions.explanation: The particle is at rest exactly when its velocity is zero.

questions.q: When differentiating a related-rates equation, every variable is treated as a function of:
questions.explanation: In related rates, quantities change over time, so each variable is differentiated with respect to time t (implicit differentiation).

questions.q: The revenue from selling x units is R(x) = 50x - 0.1x^2 dollars. What is the marginal revenue at x = 100?
A population grows according to P(t) = 200 + 30t - t^2 (t in years). At what rate is the population changing at t = 5?
The area of a circle is A = pi r^2. When r = 5, dA/dr equals:
questions.explanation: dA/dr = 2 pi r. At r = 5, this is 10 pi (the circumference).

questions.q: For a sphere V = (4/3) pi r^3, what is dV/dt in terms of dr/dt?
questions.explanation: Differentiating with respect to t: dV/dt = 4 pi r^2 (dr/dt).

questions.q: Given x^2 + y^2 = 100 with x and y functions of t, what equation relates dx/dt and dy/dt?
questions.explanation: Differentiating both sides with respect to t: 2x(dx/dt) + 2y(dy/dt) = 0.

questions.q: The volume of a cube with edge s is V = s^3. What is dV/dt in terms of ds/dt?
questions.explanation: Differentiating V = s^3 with respect to t: dV/dt = 3s^2 (ds/dt).

questions.q: The radius of a circle increases at 3 cm/s. How fast is the area increasing when r = 4 cm?
questions.explanation: dA/dt = 2 pi r (dr/dt) = 2 pi (4)(3) = 24 pi cm^2/s.

questions.q: The area of a square increases at 8 cm^2/s. How fast is the side length increasing when the side is 4 cm?
questions.explanation: A = s^2, so dA/dt = 2s(ds/dt). Then 8 = 2(4)(ds/dt) = 8(ds/dt), giving ds/dt = 1 cm/s.

questions.q: Use linearization of f(x) = sqrt(x) at a = 4 to estimate sqrt(4.1).
The tangent line to f(x) = x^3 at x = 2 is used to approximate f(2.1). The approximation is:
Use the linearization of f(x) = e^x at a = 0 to approximate e^(0.02).
Use linearization of f(x) = ln(x) at a = 1 to estimate ln(1.1).
Using L'Hopital's Rule, what is lim_{x->0} sin(x)/x?
questions.explanation: The form is 0/0. Differentiate top and bottom: lim_{x->0} cos(x)/1 = cos(0) = 1.

mock_tests.title: Practice Set B

questions.q: Using L'Hopital's Rule, what is lim_{x->0} (e^x - 1)/x?
questions.explanation: The form is 0/0. Differentiate: lim_{x->0} e^x/1 = e^0 = 1.

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x->infinity} x / e^x using L'Hopital's Rule.
questions.explanation: The form is infinity/infinity. Differentiate: lim_{x->infinity} 1/e^x = 0.

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x->2} (x^2 - 4)/(x - 2) using L'Hopital's Rule.
questions.explanation: Form 0/0: differentiate to get lim_{x->2} 2x/1 = 4. (Factoring gives the same result.)

questions.q: A tank's water depth is D(t) meters after t hours, with D'(4) = -0.5. This means at t = 4 hours the water is:
questions.explanation: A negative rate means the depth is decreasing; D'(4) = -0.5 means it drops 0.5 m per hour at that instant.

questions.q: A particle's velocity is v(t) = 3t^2 - 12. When is the particle at rest?
questions.explanation: At rest when v(t) = 3t^2 - 12 = 0, so t^2 = 4 and t = 2 (taking t >= 0).

questions.q: The demand for a product is D(p) = 500 - 4p units at price p dollars. dD/dp = -4 means:
options: demand drops by 4 units for each $1 price increase
demand rises by 4 units per dollar
questions.explanation: The derivative dD/dp = -4 gives the rate of change of demand with price: 4 fewer units sold per $1 increase.

questions.q: If the perimeter of a square is P = 4s, what is dP/dt in terms of ds/dt?
questions.explanation: Differentiating P = 4s with respect to t gives dP/dt = 4 (ds/dt).

questions.q: Using linearization of f(x) = x^(1/3) at a = 8, estimate (8.1)^(1/3).
A particle's position is s(t) = 2t^3 - 3t^2. What is its acceleration at t = 1?
Evaluate lim_{x->0} (sin(3x))/(x) using L'Hopital's Rule.
questions.explanation: Form 0/0: differentiate to get lim_{x->0} 3cos(3x)/1 = 3cos(0) = 3.

questions.q: Let f(t) be the amount of a drug (mg) in the bloodstream after t hours. If f(2) = 40 and f'(2) = -8, estimate the amount at t = 2.5 hours.
questions.explanation: Local linear approximation: f(2.5) ≈ f(2) + f'(2)(0.5) = 40 + (-8)(0.5) = 40 - 4 = 36 mg.

questions.q: Evaluate lim_{x->0} (cos(x) - 1)/x using L'Hopital's Rule.
questions.explanation: Form 0/0: differentiate to get lim_{x->0} (-sin x)/1 = -sin(0) = 0.

questions.q: A balloon's surface area A = 4 pi r^2 increases. When r = 3 and dr/dt = 2, how fast is the surface area increasing?
questions.explanation: dA/dt = 8 pi r (dr/dt) = 8 pi (3)(2) = 48 pi.

questions.q: The differential dy for y = x^2 is:
questions.explanation: By definition dy = f'(x) dx. For y = x^2, dy = 2x dx.

questions.q: A ball's height is h(t) = -4.9t^2 + 20t. What is its velocity at t = 1 second?
If y = x^2 and x changes with time, then dy/dt equals:
questions.explanation: By the Chain Rule with respect to t: dy/dt = 2x (dx/dt).

questions.q: A car's fuel efficiency E(v) (miles per gallon) depends on speed v (mph). E'(50) = -0.4 means:
options: efficiency drops 0.4 mpg for each additional mph at 50 mph
questions.explanation: E'(50) = -0.4 is the rate of change of efficiency with speed: a loss of 0.4 mpg per 1 mph increase at v = 50.

questions.q: The linear approximation of f(x) = cos(x) at a = 0 is:
Before applying L'Hopital's Rule, you must first check that the limit:
options: has an indeterminate form (0/0 or infinity/infinity)
questions.explanation: L'Hopital's Rule requires confirming the quotient is indeterminate (0/0 or infinity/infinity) before differentiating numerator and denominator.

questions.q: If W(t) is a baby's weight (kg) at age t months and W'(6) = 0.5, this means at 6 months the baby is:
questions.explanation: W'(6) = 0.5 is the instantaneous growth rate: 0.5 kg gained per month at age 6 months.
